newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH LOCAL DEFICITS NO THREAT TO EMU SHAPE -PM.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH LOCAL DEFICITS NO THREAT TO EMU SHAPE -PM.

text.p: Finnish Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said on Tuesday that an expected weakening of local government finances in the next few years would not push the public sector deficit or debt ratios beyond the limits for EMU.

"It looks like the municipal sector finances are becoming tighter," Lipponen told reporters after a meeting between himself, Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto and leaders of the Association of Local Authorities.

Asked whether this weakening could push the whole Finnish public sector deficit and/or debt ratios to GDP over the limits for membership of European economic and monetary union (EMU), Lipponen told Reuters: "No, not during the period under review." He added he was referring to the period until 2000.
"The local governments' debt to GDP will not rise noticeably," he said.
The association said local government finances would turn weaker this year despite an economic upturn, with net investments exceeding gross margins, and remain difficult throughout 1998-2001.
The entry criteria for EMU state that a country's public sector deficit must not exceed three percent of GDP and gross public debt should be no more than 60 percent of GDP.
Lipponen's five-party government has repeatedly said one of its key targets is to put the Finnish economy in shape to qualify for membership of EMU among the first group slated for start-up in 1999.
